Thanks again for the walkthrough today — that was helpful. A couple of asks so we can move procurement and internal finance forward: 

- Quick clarity on unit economics: our finance lead wants target effective cost <= $800 per 1M tokens (after any cache effects). Can you show a worked example that gets us there?
- We're expecting ~400–600M tokens/month during a 3‑month ramp (primarily chat interactions).
- Key traffic characteristics: ~70% short-chat flows (mean convo length < 64 tokens), repeatable prefixes (system prompts + common disclaimers), and 30% longer analytic generation jobs.

Attached: Acme_traffic_profile.csv with the sample distribution.

Next steps we need from you: a short worksheet that shows baseline list price -> caching assumptions -> effective $/1M, plus recommended POC scope and an estimate for a 2‑week trial. Procurement would like an initial price target to review by Nov 30.

Sam
Director of Product
Acme Health
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Holt <sam.holt@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — cost follow-up & POC budget

Sam — great to chat. Thanks for the traffic sample, that helps a lot. I attached two working artifacts: redwood_cache_assumptions_v1.pdf (narrative + hit‑rate ranges) and redwood_cost_model_v1.xlsx (live worksheet). Below is a concise worked example using conservative assumptions so finance can see the arithmetic. Please confirm if these assumptions align with your traffic and we’ll update the workbook.

Summary worked example (conservative):
- List price (baseline): $1,200 / 1M tokens
- Caching strategy applied: prefix cache for repeated system prompts + a small session KV cache for recent context
- Hit-rate assumptions used: prefix cache 25% (repeatable system & boilerplate), session KV cache 15% (recent-turn reuse) -> combined effective hit = 35% (conservative, non-overlapping simplification)
- Effective billed tokens = 65% of raw tokens
- Effective unit cost = $1,200 * 0.65 = $780 / 1M tokens (meets your $800 target)

Sensitivity: if combined hit is only 25% -> effective cost = $900/1M. If we achieve 45% combined hit -> $660/1M.

Notes & caveats:
- Hit rates will vary by endpoint and session length. Short chat flows with highly repeatable prefixes tend to see stronger prefix cache lift; long analytic jobs are less cacheable.
- We model cache memory & invalidation overheads in the workbook; for this impact calc we treated cache CPU/memory costs as included in the platform fee (shown on tab 'infra assumptions').

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll update the cost workbook with your monthly token slices (the attached CSV) and return a version with per-segment effective $/1M by EOD Thursday.
2) Schedule a 30-minute sync (Ben to run deeper through the cost model + caching knobs).
3) If the numbers look good, we propose a 2-week POC: 100M tokens, target effective <= $800/1M, instrumentation to measure actual hit rates by segment.

Attachments: redwood_cost_model_v1.xlsx, redwood_cache_assumptions_v1.pdf

— Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

- Latency SLO: we need p95 < 200ms for interactive flows; that may constrain aggressive batching.
- Procurement: Lily (cc’d) is the procurement lead; we need a simple SOW + pricing worksheet to start approval. Timeline: procurement review by Nov 30, final PO by Dec 15 if numbers align.

Sam
